newsitem.title: THAILAND: Cambodia's Hun Sen said to block guerrilla link.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia's Hun Sen said to block guerrilla link.

text.p: Cambodia's coup leader Hun Sen has sent large numbers of extra troops to western Cambodia to prevent forces of ousted Prime Minister Prince Norodom Rannariddh linking up with hardline Khmer Rouge guerrillas, breakaway Khmer Rouge sources said on Wednesday.

The sources, who were monitoring troop movements inside Cambodia by field radio, said the forces of Second Prime Minister Hun Sen had succeeded in blocking various routes between the town of Poipet on Cambodia's border with Thailand and the northwestern province of Siem Reap.

"Hun Sen ordered his troops to prevent Khmer Rouge from Anlong Veng from joining Royalist forces fighting his soldiers in Siem Reap," one of the sources, a veteran senior guerrilla commander, told Reuters.
But Thai security sources said on Wednesday morning dozens of royalist pro-Ranariddh FUNCINPEC members and their families had fled to the eastern Thai border town of Aranyaprathet, fearing a purge.
Hun Sen, who had ruled Cambodia alongside Ranariddh since U.N.-organised elections in 1993, deposed the prince and assumed sole control after bloody clashes in Phnom Penh at the weekend.

A senior Thai army source based near the hardline Khmer Rouge guerrillas' stronghold of Anlong Veng on Cambodia's northern border with Thailand said the guerrillas had been unusually quiet. He said they could be leaving jungle bases to join fighting in Cambodian cities.
"It's quiet here and we believe the scene of fighting will concentrate in Phnom Penh and other cities, where we think the Khmer Rouge are heading," he said.

Thai army commander in chief General Chetta Thanajaro told reporters there had been no major clashes yet but fierce fighting could erupt should Ranariddh loyalists manage to link up with Khmer Rouge hardliners.
The dissident Khmer Rouge sources said Hun Sen's troops gained full control of Battambang, Cambodia's second largest city, late on Tuesday.

Prom Su, pro-Ranariddh deputy governor of Cambodia's Banteay Meanchey province, who reached the Thai border town of Aranyaprathet on Wednesday morning with dozens of civilian officials of Ranariddh's faction, told Reuters that military representatives from Hun Sen's and Ranariddh's factions were holding talks near Battambang, but did not elaborate.
The dissident Khmer Rouge sources said Hun Sen's soldiers had established several checkpoints on the roads leading to the west of Cambodia from Battambang

"Hun Sen overran Battambang late on Tuesday but the situation is still tense. Ranariddh's soldiers have retreated, but they have not totally dispersed -- they have merely slowed down their fighting," the veteran commander said.
He said Hun Sen had also been warning Cambodians in Poipet that hardline Khmer Rouge guerrillas were heading there.
The Thai army source on the border said that as of Wednesday morning Poipet, opposite Aranyaprathet, remained under control of Ranariddh's forces.
The hardline Khmer Rouge forces Ranariddh's troops were reported to be trying to link up with are loyal to Khieu Samphan, who claimed last week that he had broken away from reviled chieftain Pol Pot.
The breakaway faction consists of guerrillas who defected en masse to the coalition government last year and still control a strategic area of wetern Cambodia near the Thai border.
"The conflict in the coalition has turned out serious and the fighting will be prolonged for sure. We will stay strictly neutral for the time being," a spokesman for the movement said.
